title: Sighting of Wood Storks Recorded for the First Time at Mexico’s Lake Texcoco
author: Javier Salinas Cesáreo
content:
_This article by[Javier Salinas
Cesáreo](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Javier%20Salinas%20Ces%C3%A1reo%2C%20corresponsal)
originally appeared in the [November 10, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/10/estados/registran-
avistamiento-de-ciguenas-americanas-en-el-lago-de-texcoco), Mexico’s premier
left wing daily newspaper._

**Texcoco, State of Mexico.** For the first time, a sighting of wood storks
was recorded in the Lake Texcoco Protected Natural Area; a species that
historically did not appear in reports of birds present in this ecosystem, so
its appearance opens up the possibility that this space could serve as a
temporary winter resting site during its movements.

With this record, there are now **20 bird species** that have returned to Lake
Texcoco after having stopped coming because of the drying caused by the failed
construction of the New Mexico International Airport (NAIM), or that are
arriving in the area for the first time.

Jorge Daniel Fonseca Cando, director of the Lake Texcoco Protected Natural
Area, explained that thanks to the work to recover and rehabilitate the lake,
and because more than **4,700 hectares** were flooded during this year’s rainy
season, bird migration has increased.

He explained that a few days ago, during a patrol by PROREST’s Community
Surveillance and Monitoring Brigade, they managed to spot **two juvenile wood
storks** (_Mycteria americana_) near one of the ditches in the agricultural
area of the San Salvador Atenco ejidos, Atenco.

![Two juvenile wood storks perched on bare branches at Lake
Texcoco.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/texcoco-
wood-storks-body.jpg)Photo: Brigada de Vigilancia y Monitoreo Comunitario de
Atenco 1630

He noted that the wood stork is a species that had not been recorded in the
Management Program for the Lake Texcoco Natural Resources Protection Area and
that it represents a new record.

“The sighting of this and other species is an indicator of the degree of
restoration achieved over these years, and we will continue contributing to
the recovery of the habitat of various species,” he said.

He emphasized that most of the 4,700 flooded hectares are concentrated in
bodies of water such as Lake Nabor Carrillo, with more than 900 hectares, the
area known as the airport terminal’s X, with 750, Ciénaga de San Juan, with
700, Xalapango Lagoon, with 350, and the Caracol area in Ecatepec, with 350
hectares.

He added that, with the favorable water quality conditions and the appearance
of species, there is a record of **more than 290,000 migratory and native
birds from 285 species**. Some of the species present include the swallow-
tailed gull, aplomado falcon, least grebe, streaked flycatcher, black-faced
jay, wood stork, American white pelican, American bittern, American wigeon,
rufous hummingbird and “pato bólido menor,” among others.

He recalled that this year, too, thanks to rehabilitation work and water
quality, the mexcalpique fish, a species endemic to this region, began to
increase its presence, being recorded across more than 1,200 hectares.
